en: to be unblushing; to be bold-faced

examples.en: He sat down with a cheeky smile.

examples.ko: 넉살스러운 말투 때문에 미워할 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I can't dislike him because of his cheeky way of talking.

examples.ko: 동생이 넉살스러워서 처음 만난 사람과도 금방 친해져요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is so bold and friendly that he gets close to new people fast.

examples.ko: 넉살스럽다고 해서 예의가 없는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being cheeky doesn't mean being rude.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원이 넉살스러워서 분위기가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: The new employee is so outgoing that the atmosphere got better.
He asked for pocket money with a cheeky look.

explain: 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '넉살스러워요'로 바뀌어요. 부끄러움 없이 능청스럽게 구는 모습인데, '넉살이 좋다'와 비슷하게 밉지 않고 친근한 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: That friend has a cheeky way of speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅂ' 불규칙으로 바뀐 해요체 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form, with the irregular ㅂ change.

phrases.en: Everyone relaxed because of that cheeky smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃음이나 말투 같은 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to modify nouns such as a smile or a way of speaking.

phrases.en: He spoke so cheekily that they granted his request.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 앞에서 행동 방식을 나타내는 부사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form that shows how an action is done.

explain_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '넉살스러워요'. It describes a person acting boldly and playfully without embarrassment, usually in a likable, friendly way, similar to '넉살이 좋다'.

examples.ko: 미인박명이라더니 그 배우는 너무 일찍 세상을 떠났어요.
examples.en: They say beauty is short-lived, and that actress passed away too early.
An old saying says beauties die young, but I don't believe it.
The saying 'beauty is short-lived' often appears in novels.
Grandmother said 'beauty is short-lived' and felt sorry.
They say beauty is short-lived, but she lived a long, healthy life.
Hearing the story of a short-lived beauty makes my heart ache.

explain: 아름다운 사람이 불행하거나 일찍 죽는다는 뜻의 한자성어예요. 같은 뜻으로 '가인박명'도 써요. 보통 '미인박명이라더니'처럼 안타까운 일을 말할 때 붙여요.

phrases.en: The saying 'beauty is short-lived' feels sad to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미인박명'과 같은 뜻의 한자성어예요. 조금 더 글에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Chinese-character idiom with the same meaning as 미인박명, used a bit more in writing.

phrases.en: They say beauty is short-lived, and it's truly sad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안타까운 일이 생겼을 때 이 말을 떠올리며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when remembering this saying after something sad happens.
phrases.en_equiv: as they say, beauty fades early

phrases.en: The saying 'beauty is short-lived' has existed since long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 말 자체를 소개하거나 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the saying itself.

explain_en: It is a four-character idiom about beautiful people having an unhappy or short life. '가인박명' carries the same meaning. People usually say it like '미인박명이라더니' when they feel sorry about a sad event.

examples.en: I forgot our plans yesterday and stood my friend up.
I'm really sorry for standing you up on the blind date yesterday.
I can't believe you stood me up, that's too much.

examples.ko: 또 바람맞힐 거면 미리 말해 줘요.
examples.en: If you're going to stand me up again, tell me in advance.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 저를 바람맞혀서 혼자 영화를 봤어요.
examples.en: He stood me up, so I watched the movie alone.
Who stood you up?

explain: 약속 장소에 안 나타나서 상대를 기다리게 할 때 써요. 당한 사람 입장에서는 '바람맞다'라고 해요. 친구, 연인, 소개팅처럼 사람과의 약속에 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I got stood up on a blind date yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바람맞히다'의 반대 입장으로, 약속에서 기다린 사람이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The other side of 바람맞히다, said by the person who got stood up.

phrases.en: Don't stand me up this time, and please be sure to come.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속을 지키라고 부탁하거나 당부할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to keep their appointment.

phrases.en: I broke the appointment, so my friend waited a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 일반적으로 약속을 지키지 않는다는 뜻이에요. '바람맞히다'는 안 나타나는 경우에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more general way to say breaking a promise; 바람맞히다 is for not showing up.

explain_en: Use it when you fail to show up and leave the other person waiting. From the victim's side, the word is '바람맞다'. It is common for dates, blind dates and plans with friends.

en: to be unlucky; to be unfortunate

examples.ko: 그분은 팔자가 박복하다는 말을 자주 들었어요.
examples.en: She often heard people say that her fate was unlucky.
Mother says she had a hard life because she was unlucky.
Don't think you were born unlucky.
Working all your life, you really have bad luck.

examples.ko: 할머니는 젊어서 남편을 잃고 박복했다고 한숨을 쉬셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother sighed that she had been unlucky, losing her husband young.

examples.ko: 박복한 신세를 한탄하는 인물이 드라마에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Characters who lament their unlucky lot often appear in dramas.

explain: 주로 '팔자', '신세', '인생'처럼 삶 전체를 말하는 단어와 같이 써요. 일상에서는 '운이 없다', '복이 없다'를 더 많이 말해요. 반대는 '복이 많다'이고, 다른 사람에게 직접 말하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 박복한 팔자라고 한숨을 쉬는 분이 있었어요.
phrases.en: There was a person who sighed that they had an unlucky fate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '팔자'와 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common modifier form, paired with '팔자' (fate).

phrases.example: 저는 박복하지 않아요. 좋은 가족이 있으니까요.
phrases.en: I'm not unfortunate. I have a good family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 '운이 나쁘지 않다'는 뜻을 말할 때 써요. 자기 자신에게 쓰는 것이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning 'not unlucky'; it sounds natural when said about yourself.

phrases.en: I guess I'm a person without good fortune.
phrases.nuance_ko: '박복하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 더 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '박복하다', but easier and more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It usually goes with words about life as a whole, such as '팔자', '신세' and '인생'. In daily talk people say '운이 없다' or '복이 없다' more often. The opposite is '복이 많다', and saying it directly to someone can be rude.

en: to be underprivileged; to be unfortunate; to be disadvantaged

examples.ko: 불우한 어린 시절을 보냈지만 열심히 살았어요.
examples.en: He had an unfortunate childhood but lived diligently.

examples.ko: 연말에 불우 이웃을 돕는 행사가 열려요.
examples.en: An event to help disadvantaged neighbors is held at year's end.
That writer lived an unfortunate life all his days.
Even though her circumstances were poor, she didn't give up her dream.

examples.ko: 그는 불우했던 시절을 떠올리며 눈물을 보였어요.
examples.en: He shed tears remembering his hard times.

examples.ko: 불우해 보이는 친구에게 따뜻하게 말을 건넸어요.
examples.en: I spoke warmly to a friend who seemed to be in unfortunate circumstances.

explain: 사람의 처지나 환경이 어렵고 운이 따르지 않을 때 써요. '불우 이웃', '불우 청소년'처럼 앞에 붙여서 도움이 필요한 사람을 가리키는 말로 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '어려운 이웃'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 불우한 환경에서도 그는 꿈을 포기하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: Even in a disadvantaged environment, he did not give up on his dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살기 어려운 처지나 조건을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes hard living conditions or circumstances.

phrases.example: 그 작가는 불우하게 자랐지만 좋은 글을 썼어요.
phrases.en: That writer grew up in hardship but wrote good works.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어렵고 힘든 형편에서 성장했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone grew up in difficult circumstances.

phrases.example: 저희 반은 어려운 이웃을 돕는 모임을 했어요.
phrases.en: Our class held a gathering to help neighbors in need.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '불우 이웃'보다 부드럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentler everyday alternative to 불우 이웃.

explain_en: It describes a person's situation or circumstances that are hard and unlucky. It often comes before a noun, as in '불우 이웃' or '불우 청소년', meaning people who need help. In daily talk people also say '어려운 이웃'.

en: to be heartless; to be cold-hearted

examples.ko: 비정한 현실 앞에서 그는 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: Faced with the cruel reality, he couldn't say a word.
Abandoning a child is so heartless.
Sometimes the world feels really cold.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 선수들에게 비정하다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: That coach is called heartless by his players.
It was a judgment so cool it was almost heartless.

examples.ko: 비정했던 그 사장도 마지막에는 눈물을 보였어요.
examples.en: Even that cold-hearted boss showed tears in the end.

explain: '냉정하다'는 감정에 휘둘리지 않는다는 느낌도 있지만, '비정하다'는 인정이 없다는 비판이 강해요. 사람뿐 아니라 '비정한 세상', '비정한 현실'처럼 상황에도 많이 써요. 반대로 따뜻한 사람은 '다정하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 가끔 세상이 너무 비정한 것 같아요.
phrases.en: Sometimes the world seems so heartless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람뿐 아니라 세상이나 현실에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can describe the world or reality, not just people.

phrases.en: He is cold-hearted even to his family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 사람의 인정 없음을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form used to criticize someone's lack of compassion.

phrases.en: He may seem cold, but he isn't heartless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 인정이 있다는 뜻을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying someone does have compassion.

explain_en: '냉정하다' can simply mean not being swayed by emotion, but '비정하다' strongly implies a lack of human feeling and is critical. It describes people as well as situations, as in '비정한 세상' and '비정한 현실'. The opposite, a warm person, is '다정하다'.

en: to adore and yearn for (someone) with love

examples.en: He has adored her for a long time.

examples.ko: 저는 그 가수를 사모하는 마음으로 편지를 썼어요.
examples.en: I wrote a letter with the heart of someone who adores that singer.

examples.ko: 시인은 멀리 있는 사람을 사모하며 시를 지었어요.
examples.en: The poet wrote a poem longing for someone far away.
The senior I secretly adored has graduated.
I turned away without being able to say that I adored him.
Many disciples looked up to their teacher with deep affection.

explain: '좋아하다'보다 훨씬 깊고 조심스러운, 짝사랑에 가까운 마음이에요. 일상 대화보다 시, 소설, 노래 가사에서 더 자주 나오는 오래된 느낌의 말이에요. 지금은 '좋아하다'나 '짝사랑하다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: He wrote his yearning love in a poem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊고 조심스러운 사랑의 마음을 말할 때 쓰는 꾸밈말 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for a deep and careful feeling of love.

phrases.en: A letter came from the person I used to adore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전부터 마음속으로 좋아해 온 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone you have long loved in your heart.

phrases.en: I secretly adored my senior.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하지 못하고 혼자 좋아하는 짝사랑의 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the feel of unspoken one-sided love.

explain_en: It is a far deeper, more reserved feeling than 좋아하다, close to unrequited love. It has an old-fashioned feel and appears more in poems, novels, and lyrics than in daily talk. Today people more often say 좋아하다 or 짝사랑하다.

examples.en: I was really happy to be reunited with my family after so long.
Footage of separated family members reuniting was on the news.

examples.ko: 공항에서 친구와 상봉하는 순간 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: The moment I met my friend again at the airport, I cried.
Separated families wait for the day they can reunite.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 십 년 뒤 서울에서 상봉하기로 약속했어요.
examples.en: The two promised to meet again in Seoul ten years later.
I want to see my son again, who went into the army.

explain: 오랫동안 헤어져 있던 사람을 다시 만날 때, 특히 감동적인 재회에 써요. 일상에서 약속을 잡고 보는 '만나다'와는 느낌이 달라요. '이산가족 상봉'이라는 말이 대표적이에요.

phrases.example: 이산가족 상봉 행사가 열려서 많은 사람이 울었어요.
phrases.en: A reunion event for separated families was held, and many people cried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '상봉'과 함께 쓰는 대표적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical phrase using the noun 상봉.

phrases.example: 두 형제는 상봉의 기쁨에 눈물을 흘렸어요.
phrases.en: The two brothers shed tears of joy at their reunion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜만에 만났을 때의 감동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the emotion of meeting again after a long time.

phrases.example: 저는 십 년 만에 어릴 적 친구와 상봉했어요.
phrases.en: I met my childhood friend again after ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기간 + 만에'와 함께 쓰면 오랜 이별 뒤의 재회라는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 'period + 만에', it clearly means a reunion after a long separation.

explain_en: Used when meeting someone again after a long separation, especially an emotional reunion. It feels different from '만나다', which covers ordinary meetings arranged in daily life. The typical phrase is '이산가족 상봉' (reunion of separated families).

p.n: 만났다 is natural but plain; 상봉하다 is news-style and stresses an emotional reunion.

examples.ko: 가족과의 생이별은 어린 나이에 견디기 힘든 고통이었어요.
examples.en: Being separated from my family was a pain that was hard to bear at a young age.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 집안의 반대로 생이별을 하게 됐어요.
examples.en: The two were forced apart because their families objected.
I heard he lived alone for a long time after being separated from his parents.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 형제가 생이별하는 장면을 보고 울었어요.
examples.en: I cried watching the scene in the drama where brothers are separated.

examples.ko: 생이별의 아픔을 겪은 가족이 다시 만났어요.
examples.en: The family that suffered the pain of separation met again.
Because of studying abroad, it felt like being torn away from my friend.

explain: 둘 다 살아 있는데 억지로 헤어지는 경우에 쓰고, 죽어서 헤어지는 '사별'과 달라요. 가족이나 연인처럼 가까운 사이에 쓰고, '생이별하다'나 '생이별을 하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I was forcibly separated from my family because of the war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '생이별'에 '하다'를 붙인 동사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form made by adding '하다' to the noun.

phrases.example: 전쟁으로 생이별한 가족이 오랜만에 다시 만났어요.
phrases.en: A family that had been forcibly separated by the war met again after a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 억지로 헤어진 사람들을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form describes people who were forcibly parted.
phrases.en_equiv: a family that was forcibly separated

phrases.example: 가족과 떨어져 사는 생이별의 아픔은 정말 커요.
phrases.en: The pain of being separated from one's family is truly great.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'와 함께 헤어진 사람의 슬픔을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '의', it describes the sorrow of those who were separated.

explain_en: It is used when two people who are both alive are forced apart, which differs from '사별' (parting through death). It applies to close ties like family or lovers and is said as '생이별하다' or '생이별을 하다'.

en: to cut off relationship; to break relations

examples.en: He cut ties with his older brother over a money issue.
I've cut off my parents and live alone.
It hurts that I've broken off with an old friend.
It's been over ten years since we cut ties.
Even if you're angry, don't cut off your family.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 크게 다투고 의절해 버렸어요.
examples.en: The two had a big fight and ended up cutting ties.

explain: 가족이나 친척, 아주 가까운 사이와 관계를 끊는다는 무거운 말이에요. '~와/과 의절하다'로 써요. 단순히 연락이 뜸해진 정도가 아니에요. 친구 사이에는 '절교하다'도 써요.

phrases.en: Those two cut ties long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관계가 완전히 끊어진 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a relationship that is completely broken.

phrases.example: 아버지와 의절하고 지낸 지 십 년이 됐어요.
phrases.en: It has been ten years since I cut ties with my father.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연락 없이 지내는 상태가 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the break in contact continues over time.

phrases.en: I ended my friendship with that friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족이 아니라 친구 사이에서 관계를 끊을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for ending a friendship, not a family tie.

explain_en: It is a heavy word for cutting off a relationship with family, relatives or very close people, used as '~와/과 의절하다'. It is more than just losing touch. Between friends, '절교하다' is also used.

en: to be waggish; to be humorous; to be jesting

examples.en: My grandfather has such a humorous way of talking.
He made the children laugh with a comical expression.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 익살맞게 연기해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That actor acts in a playful way and is very popular.

examples.ko: 익살맞은 동생 덕분에 가족 모임이 늘 즐거워요.
examples.en: Thanks to my funny younger sibling, family gatherings are always fun.

examples.ko: 사진 속 강아지의 모습이 너무 익살맞아 보여요.
examples.en: The puppy in the photo looks so comical.

examples.ko: 친구는 익살맞아서 어디에서나 사람들이 곁에 모여요.
examples.en: My friend is so jocular that people gather around wherever he goes.

explain: '웃기다'보다 말이나 표정이 재치 있고 정다운 느낌이에요. '익살스럽다'도 같은 느낌으로 쓰여요. 사람의 말투, 표정, 동작에 많이 써요.

phrases.en: He spoke humorously and made everyone laugh.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재치 있고 정답게 말하는 방식을 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes speaking in a witty, endearing way.

phrases.en: The child's dance is comical.
phrases.nuance_ko: '익살맞다'와 비슷한 느낌으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word with a similar feel to 익살맞다.

phrases.example: 곰 인형이 익살맞은 동작으로 춤을 춰요.
phrases.en: The teddy bear dances with funny movements.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃음을 주는 몸짓을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe gestures that bring a smile.

explain_en: Compared with '웃기다' (funny), it suggests witty, endearing words or expressions. '익살스럽다' is used in a similar way. It is mostly used for a person's speech, face or gestures.

examples.en: The king especially favored that minister.
The pupil the teacher favors was chosen as the representative.
The boss dotes on the youngest who works well.
The granddaughter my grandfather doted on got married.

examples.ko: 윗사람이 한 사람만 총애하면 팀 분위기가 나빠져요.
examples.en: If a superior favors only one person, the team atmosphere gets worse.
She is a child so diligent that the teachers dote on her.

explain: 윗사람이 아랫사람을 특별히 아낄 때 쓰기 때문에, 학생이 선생님께 쓰면 어색해요. 같은 마음을 일상에서는 '아끼다'나 '예뻐하다'로 말해요. 반대로 받는 쪽에서는 '총애를 받다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The official the king favors came into the palace.
phrases.nuance_ko: '총애하다'를 꾸미는 말로 쓴 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun.

phrases.en: Grandma cherishes her youngest grandson a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '총애하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday word used instead of 총애하다.

phrases.en: The teacher is fond of that student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아랫사람을 귀여워하는 마음을 일상 대화에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in daily talk for fondness toward someone younger or junior.

explain_en: It is used when a superior especially cherishes someone below, so it sounds odd if a student says it about a teacher. In daily speech the same feeling is expressed with '아끼다' or '예뻐하다'. From the receiving side, you say '총애를 받다'.

examples.en: That child is the same as my own flesh and blood.
Because we're blood relatives, sometimes it hurts even more.

examples.ko: 그는 혈육 하나 없이 혼자 살아왔어요.
examples.en: He has lived alone without a single blood relative.
I cried when I met my blood relative after a long time.
The bond between blood relatives isn't easily broken.

examples.ko: 헤어졌던 혈육과 오십 년 만에 다시 만났어요.
examples.en: He met the relative he had been separated from again after fifty years.

explain: 부모, 형제, 자식처럼 피로 이어진 가족을 말해요. '가족'은 함께 사는 사람까지 넓게 가리키지만 '혈육'은 핏줄이라는 점이 중요해요. 조금 글 같고 감정이 실린 말이라서 '혈육의 정'처럼 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '피붙이'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 혈육의 정은 쉽게 끊을 수 없어요.
phrases.en: The bond of blood relatives cannot be easily cut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족 사이의 깊은 정을 글처럼 감정을 담아 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A literary, emotional phrase for the deep bond between blood relatives.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is my only blood relative.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까운 가족이 한 명밖에 없다는 마음을 강조할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses that only one close family member is left.

phrases.en: I am looking for the family member I was separated from.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 못 만난 핏줄의 가족을 찾는 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in stories about finding a long-lost blood relative.

explain_en: It refers to family tied by blood, such as parents, siblings and children. '가족' can include people who simply live together, but '혈육' stresses the blood tie. It is a bit literary and emotional, often used in '혈육의 정'. A similar word is '피붙이'.

examples.en: The two of them got married last spring.

examples.ko: 혼인하는 두 사람에게 축하 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: I congratulated the couple who were getting married.
To be legally married, you have to submit documents.
They got married and live in the countryside.

examples.ko: 스무 살에 혼인한 할머니가 옛날이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother, who married at twenty, told me old stories.
I have someone to marry, so I am preparing to move.

explain: 일상에서는 '결혼하다'를 훨씬 많이 말해요. '혼인하다'는 법, 서류, 옛날이야기처럼 격식 있는 글에서 자주 나와요. '혼인 신고'처럼 서류에 쓰는 말과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: We filed our marriage registration at the district office yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼인하다'와 잘 어울리는 서류 관련 표현이고, 법적으로 부부가 되는 절차를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A document-related phrase that pairs well with '혼인하다'; it refers to the legal procedure of becoming a married couple.

phrases.example: 혼인한 지 오 년이 된 부부예요.
phrases.en: They are a couple who have been married for five years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼인하다'를 꾸미는 말로 바꾼 형태라서 글이나 서류에서 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of '혼인하다', which sounds natural in writing and formal documents.

phrases.en: The two of them are getting married next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 일상 대화에서는 '혼인하다'보다 '결혼하다'를 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same thing, but '결혼하다' is much more common than '혼인하다' in everyday conversation.

explain_en: In everyday talk Koreans say '결혼하다' far more often. 혼인하다 shows up in law, paperwork and old stories. It pairs well with official terms like '혼인 신고' (marriage registration).
